name: DataTable
description: A powerful compound data table component built on TanStack Table with server-side pagination, sorting, filtering, column visibility, row selection, column reordering via drag-and-drop, column pinning (freezing columns to an edge), inline cell editing, and loading states. Uses the useDataTable hook for centralized state management. Designed for complex backoffice tables that require advanced interactivity — for simple static tables, use the Table component instead.

blocks.content:
The `useDataTable` hook centralizes **all** table state in one place. It manages pagination, sorting, column filters, column visibility, column order, and row selection. It returns state values, setters, and `onXxxChange` aliases that match DataTable prop names — so `{...tableState}` wires everything up automatically.

We recommend using the hook for all DataTable usage. However, if you prefer, you can manage state yourself with `useState` and pass props individually to `<DataTable>` — the component accepts both approaches.

### What the hook manages

The hook handles ALL table state internally. You do NOT need separate `useState` calls for any of these:

- **pagination** — `{ pageIndex, pageSize }` — current page and rows per page
- **sorting** — `[{ id, desc }]` — which columns are sorted and their direction
- **columnFilters** — `[{ id, value }]` — active filters per column
- **columnVisibility** — `{ [columnId]: boolean }` — which columns are visible/hidden
- **columnOrder** — `string[]` — display order of columns
- **selectedRows** — `Record<string, TData>` — selected rows keyed by ID, with full row data as values

All of these are spread onto `<DataTable>` via `{...tableState}`. The only props you still pass manually are:
- `columns` — your column definitions
- `data` — the fetched data array
- `pageCount` — total pages from API (`Math.ceil(total / pageSize)`)
- `enableRowSelection` — boolean to enable checkboxes (config, not state)
- `rowSelectionKey` — required when `enableRowSelection` is true, a function returning a unique ID per row
- `enableColumnReordering` — boolean to enable drag-and-drop (config, not state)
- `isLoading` / `loadingRowCount` — loading state you manage from your fetch logic
### Options

rows: Initial number of rows per page.
Prefix for URL params when multiple tables share the same page. Example: 'shipments' produces ?shipments_page=1&shipments_pageSize=10.
Next.js router instance. When provided, table state (pagination, sorting, filters) is synced to the URL automatically.
Next.js searchParams for reading initial state from URL on first render.

blocks.content:
### Returns

For each state the hook returns three things: the value, a setter, and an `onXxxChange` alias. The alias is the same reference as the setter — it exists so `{...tableState}` maps directly to DataTable prop names.

rows: Setter for pagination state. Both are the same reference.
Object mapping column IDs to boolean.
Array of column IDs for display order.
Object mapping row IDs to full row data. Access selected IDs via Object.keys(tableState.selectedRows) or full data via Object.values(tableState.selectedRows). Selection persists across pages.
True while a URL transition is pending (only relevant when router is provided).
Serializes pagination, sorting, and filters into URLSearchParams for API calls.

blocks.content: ### Basic usage

const tableState = useDataTable();

<DataTable columns={columns} data={data} pageCount={pageCount} {...tableState}>
  <DataTableContent />
  <DataTablePagination />
</DataTable>
### With row selection
### With URL synchronization

### DataTableContent

Renders the table body with headers, rows, loading skeletons, and empty state. Must be placed inside `<DataTable>`. Reads table state from internal context — no props needed.

### DataTableToolbar

A flex container for filter inputs, action buttons, and view options above the table. Place inside `<DataTable>` before `<DataTableContent>`.

rows: Filter inputs, buttons, DataTableViewOptions, or any controls.

blocks.content:
### DataTableColumnHeader

Removed. Use a plain string for `header` in your column definition — the table automatically renders sort buttons and drag handles based on `enableSorting` and `enableColumnReordering`.

rows: TanStack Table column instance from header render function.
Display text for the column header.

blocks.content:
### DataTableViewOptions

Dropdown menu button (Settings2 icon) to toggle column visibility. Shows columns with `enableHiding !== false`. Place inside `<DataTableToolbar>`. Reads table instance from context when inside `<DataTable>`.

### DataTablePagination

Pagination controls with rows-per-page selector, page indicator, and navigation buttons (first/prev/next/last). The rows-per-page selector automatically includes the current pageSize in its options even if it's not in the default list. Shows selected row count when rows are selected. Place as the last child inside `<DataTable>`. Hide during loading: `{!isLoading && <DataTablePagination />}`.

rows: Page size options in the rows-per-page selector. The current pageSize is always included automatically.
Shows 'X of Y row(s) selected' when rows are selected.

blocks.content:
### DataTableSelectionBar

A fixed bottom bar that appears when rows are selected. Shows the selection count, developer-provided bulk action buttons (children), and a Deselect button. Automatically hides when no rows are selected. Responsive: on mobile it uses two rows (label + horizontally-scrollable actions); on desktop it renders as a single row with dividers. Place inside `<DataTable>` after `<DataTablePagination>`.

rows: Bulk action buttons (e.g., Delete, Export). Rendered between the selection count and the Deselect button.
Additional CSS classes merged with the default bar styling.

blocks.content: #### Usage

<DataTable
  columns={columns}
  data={data}
  pageCount={pageCount}
  enableRowSelection
  rowSelectionKey={(row) => String(row.id)}
  {...tableState}
>
  <DataTableToolbar>...</DataTableToolbar>
  <DataTableContent />
  {!isLoading && <DataTablePagination />}
  <DataTableSelectionBar>
    <Button variant="destructive" size="sm" onClick={handleBulkDelete}>
      <Trash className="mr-1 h-4 w-4" /> Delete
    </Button>
    <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={handleExport}>
      <Download className="mr-1 h-4 w-4" /> Export
    </Button>
  </DataTableSelectionBar>
</DataTable>

### DataTableEditBar

Fixed bottom bar shown when there are pending (unsaved) cell edits. Displays the count ('N changes made') and Save / Discard buttons. 'Save changes' commits all pending edits via onCellsEdited; if that callback rejects (e.g. validation failed) the bar stays open and the edits are kept. 'Discard changes' clears the pending edits and triggers onDiscardEdits. Auto-hides when there are no pending edits. Responsive (two rows on mobile, single row on desktop). Place inside <DataTable> after <DataTablePagination>. Only relevant when enableCellEditing is true.

Inline cell editing lets users edit values directly in the table. It is opt-in: set `enableCellEditing` on `<DataTable>` and mark editable columns with `enableEditing: true`. Requires `rowSelectionKey` (the row identity used to track edits). All edits flow through a single save action — nothing reaches your `data` until the user clicks 'Save changes' in DataTableEditBar.

### Enabling

- `enableCellEditing` on `<DataTable>` turns the feature on.
- `enableEditing: true` on a column makes its cells editable — a column-level flag at the same level as `enableSorting` / `enableHiding` (NOT inside `meta`).
- Add `<DataTableEditBar />` inside `<DataTable>` so the user can save/discard.
- Provide `rowSelectionKey` (required when editing is enabled).

### Interaction model

- **Click** or **Tab** into an editable cell to select it (a faint box on hover hints which cells are editable). Use the **arrow keys** to move the selection between editable cells (roving tabindex; clamped to the current page).
- **Double click**, or **Enter** / **F2** on a selected cell, to edit it.
- **Enter** or **leaving the cell** stages the change as pending (highlighted with a faint primary tint). **Escape** cancels.
- Pending changes accumulate across cells. Nothing is applied to `data` until the user presses **Save changes** in DataTableEditBar.
- **Save changes** calls `onCellsEdited({ data, changes })`. **Discard changes** clears the pending buffer and calls `onDiscardEdits()`.

### editCell context

The `editCell` renderer fully controls commit via the functions it receives (no automatic key/blur handling, so portal-based editors like Select don't commit prematurely).

rows: Current draft value of the cell.
Updates the draft value (does not commit).
Stages `value` as a pending change. Pass the value explicitly to avoid stale-closure bugs (e.g. onValueChange={(v) => stage(v)}).
Cancels the edit and reverts to the value in data.

blocks.content:
### Saving and validation

Validation is the consumer's responsibility. Validate inside `onCellsEdited`; to reject a save, set `cellErrors` and return a rejected Promise — the pending edits are kept and the invalid cells turn destructive (message shown in a tooltip). Clear `cellErrors` on a successful save AND in `onDiscardEdits`, otherwise a stale error stays after the cell reverts. Use the `changes` diff to build your API request and the `data` payload for an optimistic setData.

### Constraints

- **Single field per column.** Editing writes the new value to the column's `accessorKey`, so every editable column must have an `accessorKey`. A dev-only `console.warn` fires if `enableEditing` is set on a column without one.
- **Composite cells are not editable.** Cells that render several data points without a single `accessorKey` cannot be edited in this model — do not set `enableEditing` on them. If you need to edit one of their fields, give that field its own editable column with an `accessorKey`.
- **Custom editor styling is the consumer's job.** The default text editor already blends into the cell. For `editCell` editors, style the control to blend — e.g. a SelectTrigger with `className="h-auto border-0 px-0 py-0 shadow-none focus:ring-0"`.

Pin (freeze) columns to an edge so they stay visible while the rest of the table scrolls horizontally. Set `pin: "left"` or `pin: "right"` on a column definition — a column-level flag at the same level as `enableSorting` / `enableEditing`. It is fully declarative: there is no DataTable-level prop to enable it and no extra state to manage.

### Behavior

- Pinned columns are anchored to their edge with `position: sticky`; the center columns scroll between them.
- Left- and right-pinned columns are grouped **consecutively** at their edge in declaration order. You cannot pin a lone middle column — the TanStack model always pulls pinned columns to an edge, so non-consecutive / middle pinning is impossible by construction.
- A subtle shadow appears on the seam **only while there is scrolled-away content** on that side (it fades out at the start/end of the scroll).
- When any column is pinned, the table is given a `min-width` (sum of column widths) and `table-layout: fixed` so it reliably overflows and the sticky offsets line up to the pixel. Tables with **no** pinned columns are unaffected.
- Pinned columns don't show the drag handle (they can't be reordered), and keyboard navigation between editable cells scrolls the selected cell clear of the pinned edges.

rows: Freezes the column to the left or right edge. Requires the column to have a stable `id` or string `accessorKey`. Pinned columns are grouped consecutively at their edge.

blocks.content: Columns use the `ColumnDef<TData>[]` type, re-exported from the design system so consumers never need `@tanstack/react-table` directly. Common patterns:

Use `DateRangePicker` (from `@traxion-global/design-system/react`) for date range filters in `DataTableToolbar`. It replaces the manual Calendar+Popover+Button pattern with a single self-contained component that handles the trigger button, popover open/close, Apply/Clear logic, and locale formatting. For a single-date filter use `DatePicker`. **Never use `<input type="date">`** — it bypasses design system styling, locale support, and accessibility.
For time-of-day filters (e.g. filtering by hour in a report or log table), use `TimePicker` in the toolbar:

props.name: columns
props.description: Array of TanStack Table column definitions. Import ColumnDef from the design system. Each column defines header, accessorKey or accessorFn, optional cell renderer, and column-level features (enableSorting, enableHiding, size).

props.name: data
props.description: Array of row data objects. Typically fetched from an API. The data must match the shape expected by the column definitions.

props.name: pageCount
props.description: Total number of pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(totalItems / pageSize). Required because DataTable uses server-side (manual) pagination.

props.name: pagination
props.description: Controlled pagination state: { pageIndex: number, pageSize: number }. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: onPaginationChange
props.description: Pagination change handler. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: sorting
props.description: Controlled sorting state. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}. If not provided, managed internally.

props.name: onSortingChange
props.description: Sorting change handler. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: columnFilters
props.description: Controlled column filters state. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}. If not provided, managed internally.

props.name: onColumnFiltersChange
props.description: Column filters change handler. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: selectedRows
props.description: Controlled selected rows state. Maps row IDs (from rowSelectionKey) to full row data objects. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}. Selection persists across pages.

props.name: onSelectedRowsChange
props.description: Selected rows change handler. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: enableRowSelection
props.description: Enables row selection. This is a config flag, NOT state — pass it directly (not from the hook). Set to true to allow all rows, or pass a function for conditional selection per row. Requires rowSelectionKey when enabled.

props.name: rowSelectionKey
props.description: Required when enableRowSelection is true. A function that returns a unique string identifier for each row (e.g., (row) => String(row.id)). Used to track selection across pages.

props.name: columnVisibility
props.description: Controlled column visibility state. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}. If not provided, managed internally.

props.name: onColumnVisibilityChange
props.description: Column visibility change handler. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: columnOrder
props.description: Controlled column order state. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}. If not provided, managed internally.

props.name: onColumnOrderChange
props.description: Column order change handler. Provided by useDataTable via {...tableState}.

props.name: enableColumnReordering
props.description: Enables drag-and-drop column reordering. This is a config flag, NOT state — pass it directly (not from the hook). When true, columns with a string header automatically render a GripVertical drag handle.

props.name: enableCellEditing
props.description: Enables inline cell editing. This is a config flag, NOT state — pass it directly. Columns opt in individually with enableEditing: true. Requires rowSelectionKey (used as the row identity). See the 'Cell Editing' section for the full model.

props.name: onCellsEdited
props.type: (payload: { data: TData[]; changes: CellEdit<TData>[] }) => void | Promise<void>
props.description: Called ONLY when the user saves the pending edits via DataTableEditBar. Receives the current page `data` with the changes applied (pass to your setData) and the `changes` diff (build your API request — each entry has rowId, columnId, previousValue, value, row). Return a Promise to make the save transactional: if it rejects, the pending edits are kept so the user can correct them (typically you also set cellErrors).

props.name: onDiscardEdits
props.description: Called when the user discards the pending edits via DataTableEditBar. Use it to clear consumer-owned state derived from the edits — in particular cellErrors set during a previous failed save, which would otherwise remain after the cells revert to their original values.

props.name: cellErrors
props.description: Marks cells as invalid from outside. Shape: { [rowId]: { [columnId]: message } } where rowId comes from rowSelectionKey. Invalid cells are painted with the destructive color and show the message in a tooltip. The consumer owns this state (set it from your validation, clear it in onDiscardEdits / on successful save).

props.name: isLoading
props.description: When true, DataTableContent renders skeleton rows instead of data. Headers are still visible. Hide DataTablePagination during loading: {!isLoading && <DataTablePagination />}.

props.name: loadingRowCount
props.description: Number of skeleton rows to render when isLoading is true.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Custom empty state rendered when data array is empty and isLoading is false. Defaults to NoDataMessage component.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes merged with default 'space-y-4' wrapper styling.

props.name: children
props.description: Compound children. Use DataTableToolbar, DataTableContent, DataTablePagination, and DataTableViewOptions as children. If no children are provided, renders DataTableContent by default.

accessibility.role: table (native HTML semantics via the underlying Table component)
accessibility.keyboard: Tab navigates through interactive elements (sort buttons, checkboxes, action buttons, pagination controls). Sort buttons toggle direction on Enter/Space. Drag handles support keyboard reordering via arrow keys. Pagination buttons are keyboard accessible with sr-only labels. When cell editing is enabled, editable cells use a roving tabindex: Tab enters the editable grid, arrow keys move the selection between editable cells (clamped to the current page), Enter/F2 start editing a selected cell, and Escape cancels editing or deselects.
accessibility.aria: Row selection state conveyed via data-[state=selected] on TableRow. Checkbox columns use aria-label for screen readers. Drag handles use aria-label='Drag to reorder column'. Pagination buttons have sr-only text ('Go to first page', 'Go to previous page', etc.). Sort direction indicated visually via icons (ChevronUp for asc, ChevronDown for desc, ChevronsUpDown for unsorted).
accessibility.notes: The table renders inside a 'rounded-md border' container. Loading state preserves table headers and renders animated skeleton bars for body cells. Empty state renders a full-width NoDataMessage inside the table body — headers remain visible so users understand the page context. When enableColumnReordering is true, DndContext is only initialized after client-side hydration to prevent SSR mismatches.

recommendations.description: Use the useDataTable() hook for state management — it handles pagination, sorting, filters, column visibility, column order, and row selection. Spread it onto DataTable: {...tableState}
Always include <DataTablePagination /> — every backoffice table must have pagination
Hide pagination during loading: {!isLoading && <DataTablePagination />}
Reset pagination to page 0 when filters change: useEffect(() => { tableState.setPagination(prev => ({ ...prev, pageIndex: 0 })); }, [tableState.columnFilters])

Use useDebouncedCallback for text filter inputs to avoid excessive API calls while the user types. This is the only filter type that needs local useState — the local state intentionally lags behind the actual filter for debounce. All other filter controls (Select, DateRangePicker, TimePicker) should derive their value directly from tableState.columnFilters.
Set enableSorting: false and enableHiding: false on action and checkbox columns

Columns are non-sortable by default. Add `enableSorting: true` on any column that should be sortable — the table automatically renders the sort button. Only use a render function header for fully custom headers (like select checkboxes or action buttons).

Use the column `id` field to match the API field name used for sorting and filtering (e.g., id: 'firstName'). The string `header` value is used as the display label everywhere (ViewOptions menu, drag overlay) — so id and header can differ.
Include tableState.sorting and tableState.columnFilters in your useEffect dependencies when they are used
Use the cell render function with row.original to access the full row data object for custom cell content
Use mixed-content cells (multiple lines in one cell) for related data that doesn't justify its own column
Use icons from lucide-react only — never emoji, unicode, or other icon libraries
Place DataTableViewOptions inside DataTableToolbar for consistent layout

Access selected rows via Object.values(tableState.selectedRows) for full row data, or Object.keys(tableState.selectedRows) for IDs — no separate useState needed. Always provide rowSelectionKey when enableRowSelection is true.

Use DataTableSelectionBar for bulk actions on selected rows — it provides a fixed bottom bar with selection count, action buttons, and a Deselect button. Place it inside <DataTable> after <DataTablePagination>.
Use DateRangePicker for date range filters in DataTableToolbar — it replaces the manual Calendar+Popover pattern with a single component.
Use DatePicker for single-date filters in DataTableToolbar.
Use TimePicker for time-of-day filters in DataTableToolbar or filter panels.
Never use <input type="date"> or <input type="time"> directly — always use DatePicker, DateRangePicker, or TimePicker.
Enable cell editing with enableCellEditing on DataTable + enableEditing: true per column. Always include <DataTableEditBar /> and rowSelectionKey when editing is enabled.
Validate edits inside onCellsEdited; to block a save, set cellErrors and return a rejected Promise — the invalid cells turn destructive and the pending edits are kept.
Clear cellErrors in onDiscardEdits and after a successful save, so a stale error doesn't persist once the cell reverts to its original value.
Use the `changes` diff from onCellsEdited to build your API request (PATCH only what changed); use the `data` payload for an optimistic setData.

For editCell custom editors, style the control to blend into the cell (e.g. a SelectTrigger with className 'h-auto border-0 px-0 py-0 shadow-none focus:ring-0'), and pass the value explicitly to stage(value).

Pin columns with pin: 'left' or pin: 'right' to keep identity/selection columns and action columns visible while wide tables scroll horizontally. Pinned columns must have a stable id or string accessorKey.

When pinning, give columns enough width (TanStack size) that the total exceeds the container, otherwise the table fits and there is nothing to scroll. Truncate long text per-column with a `truncate` cell so columns keep their width.
Truncation is a per-column concern: add a cell renderer with a `truncate` div (and a title attribute for the full value) on text columns that can overflow — the DataTable does not truncate for you.
Don't use DataTable for simple static tables — use the Table component instead

Don't create separate useState() calls for pagination, sorting, filters, column visibility, column order, or selected rows — useDataTable() manages all of these. If you prefer custom handlers, you can pass props individually instead of using the hook

Don't create a separate useState to track the current value of filter controls like Select, DateRangePicker, or TimePicker. Derive their value directly from tableState.columnFilters — it's already the source of truth. Example: value={tableState.columnFilters.find(f => f.id === 'role')?.value as string ?? 'all'}. The only exception is text inputs using useDebouncedCallback, where local state is intentional so the input lags behind the actual filter.
Don't import from @tanstack/react-table directly — import ColumnDef, Row, Column from @traxion-global/design-system/react
Don't use client-side pagination — DataTable is designed for server-side (manual) pagination only
Don't forget to pass pageCount — it is required for server-side pagination to work
Don't show DataTablePagination while isLoading is true — it will show stale data
Don't use a render function header on columns that should be sortable or reorderable — render function headers bypass the automatic sort button and drag handle. Use a plain string header instead.
Don't create separate columns for closely related data (city + state + country) — use a multi-line cell instead
Don't hardcode color values — use semantic Tailwind classes (text-muted-foreground, text-destructive, etc.)

Don't enable editing on composite/display columns or any column without an accessorKey — the edit has nowhere to be written (a dev warning is emitted). Editing is single-field-per-column; give an editable sub-field its own column with an accessorKey.
Don't expect edits to apply immediately — all edits are pending until the user saves via DataTableEditBar (onCellsEdited only fires on save, never on Enter alone).
Don't rely on editCell's `value` for the committed value in synchronous editors (e.g. Select) — pass the chosen value explicitly to stage(value) to avoid stale-closure bugs.
Don't try to pin a non-consecutive or middle column — pinning only groups columns at the left or right edge. Set pin only on columns that belong at an edge.
Don't pin a column without a stable id or string accessorKey — the pinning state is derived from the column id and won't resolve otherwise.
